Title: CEMP-015
RequirementSummary: Treatment of Soil - Wastewater Management Performance criteria and verification testing The following performance criteria must be met for soils that have been treated using neutralisation: - A suitably qualified person will be present on-site durin…
Requirement:
Treatment of Soil - Wastewater Management
Performance criteria and verification testing
The following performance criteria must be met for soils that have been treated using neutralisation:
- A suitably qualified person will be present on-site during the treatment of all acid sulfate soils to visually confirm the required rate and quantity of agricultural lime (or equivalent) has been mixed sufficiently with the processed materials.
- Treatment records must be maintained and include the day, time and amount of neutralising reagent used per batch / or layer.
- A certificate or verification letter will be prepared confirming the ASS has been adequately neutralised for each batch to be disposed of off-site or re-used on-site and should include the following:
     - Stockpile identification number
     - Reference to relevant report or chemical assessment
     - Location of the treatment area
     - A soil description
     - The results of the validation testing
     - Liming requirements have been met.
- If soil materials are deemed to be visually inconsistent with the original sampling and associated ASS assessment, the following field screening and criteria will be implemented:
     - Sampling is to be undertaken within 24-48 hours following liming of the ASS material.
     - Composite sampling is preferred rather than a single grab sample.
     - Post-neutralisation, the field pH is to be greater than 6.5, and the pHFOX is to be greater than or equal to 5.5.
     - Excess neutralising agents should stay within the treated soil until all acid generation reactions are complete and the soil has no further capacity to generate acidity.
     - Collect SCR validation samples. SCR validation sample results should show net acidity equal (including ANC) equal to or below zero.
     - Further liming is required if the ASS soils did not achieve the verification criteria (refer to Step 5).
     - The minimum soil sampling densities outlined in Table 5 must be used to verify post-neutralisation effectiveness.
     - If the stockpile has been over-limed, additional untreated soil exhibiting the same or similar characteristics will be mixed with the material to correct this, followed by further verification testing.
     - Once the materials have been verified as being neutralised, they will be transferred to the “Treated” Area for beneficial re-use or off-site disposal.
SourceReference: CEMP (B) Annex C Section 5.9.2 Treatment Process for Soils

Title: ADR-003
RequirementSummary: The following standards apply under these accepted development requirements: 1. Development work minimises impacts to waterways and fish habitats. 2. In tidal waterways, tidal exchange and flow at the site must not be impeded for more than 21 days.…
Requirement:
The following standards apply under these accepted development requirements:
1. Development work minimises impacts to waterways and fish habitats.
2. In tidal waterways, tidal exchange and flow at the site must not be impeded for more than 21 days. After 21 days, tidal flushing must be restored (tidal flushing is recommended for a minimum of 48 hours).
3. Excavation work in un-bunded tidal areas is to be scheduled to occur within two hours either side of low tide.
4. Works do not commence during times of elevated flow and in un-bunded tidal areas is to be scheduled to occur within two hours either side of low tide.
5. Where works are for the replacement of an existing waterway barrier work, the defunct waterway barrier work is to be completely removed as soon as possible and within four weeks of the completion of the replacement works.
6. Replacement of existing structures complies with the requirements for the construction of a new structure, under the relevant section of this code.
7. Other than spoil deliberately used for re-profiling to restore bed and banks to natural profiles, spoil from excavation is removed from tidal land and other wetlands and waterways.
8. Soil and sediment must not be removed from areas subject to quarantine restrictions e.g. declared fire ant areas.
9. All material used in the works are acid sulfate soil (ASS) free and potential acid sulfate soils (PASS) free or have been treated to accepted standards to prevent movement of sediment, runoff and leachate to fish habitats (guidance for current accepted standards can be found in the QASSTM: Soil management guidelines).
10. Impacts on water quality are to be minimised by undertaking the works to the standard set out in the current version of the Best Practice Erosion and Sediment Control, published by the International Erosion Control Association, Australasia.
11. Provisions are made to minimise the risk of fish kills arising from the works e.g. through entrapment of fish upstream or between works.
12. In the event that fish that have been trapped by the works, fish salvage activities in accordance with the Fisheries Queensland Guidelines for Fish Salvage (available at www.daf.qld.gov.au) are implemented immediately.
13. Fish kills must be reported to the Department of Environment and Science on 1300 130 372.
14. For any part of the waterway bed or banks adjacent to the works that has been altered by the waterway barrier works, the site is restored and/or rehabilitated so that as a minimum:
- Stability and profiles of the bed and banks are re-instated to natural stream profiles and stability within five (5) business days of the completion of the works
- The waterway bed is retained with natural substrate or reconstructed with substrate comparable to the natural substrate size and consistency
- Site conditions allow the rapid re-establishment of native vegetation and cover or native species are replanted to re-establish the natural plant community
15. Maintenance works on culverts that are for re-sleeving can only be undertaken once on any given culvert cell.

Title: ADR-004
RequirementSummary: Minimise impacts to fisheries resources and fish habitats by taking the following actions: - Minimise disturbance to the instream bed and banks e.g. use geofabric as a work base, or construct a work platform above the substrate. - If it is necessary…
Requirement:
Minimise impacts to fisheries resources and fish habitats by taking the following actions:
- Minimise disturbance to the instream bed and banks e.g. use geofabric as a work base, or construct a work platform above the substrate.
- If it is necessary to remove vegetation, aim to cut vegetation no lower than ground level and leave the root in the ground to aid in stabilisation. If deep excavation is required during construction the roots may only be removed within the construction footprint area
- Minimise the area of land disturbed or compacted e.g. construct a work platform above the substrate
- Ensure the least volume of soil or sediment is disturbed
- Limit the use of machinery within waterways
- Use machinery no greater than the capacity required for the purpose
- Implement sediment and erosion protection measures
- Undertake works at times that minimise disruption to fish migration and the flowering and fruiting of marine plants
Works should be managed to avoid fish stress. Signs of distressed fish may include gasping at the surface, rapid breathing, rolling or lethargy.

Recommendation 3: Cultural Heritage Induction for Contractors
Cultural Heritage Inductions deal with the physical heritage that may be encountered within the Study Areas. The implementation of this Cultural Heritage Induction procedure aims to avoid further harm to Aboriginal cultural heritage. It is recommended that all relevant staff and contractors undertake a Cultural Heritage Induction, with input from the Danggan Balun People, prior to construction activities. The agreed upon induction will cover cultural awareness, the basic legislative requirements regarding the Aboriginal
Cultural Heritage Act 2003 (Qld), the basic principles of identifying Aboriginal Cultural Heritage and appropriate protocols for the management of finds and human remains. The induction should also be delivered to contractors involved with ground disturbing works in the Study Areas.
If this cultural heritage induction for contractors is required before the quoted Cultural Heritage Induction Video is completed, an alternative cultural heritage induction is able to be organised between Danggan Balun and TMR.

Requirement:
Recommendation 5: Aboriginal Human Remains
It is highly unlikely that human remains will be located at any stage during works within the Study Area. If human remains are identified, all works must halt in the immediate area to prevent any further impacts to the remains and TMR must adhere to their “How to manage the discovery of Human Remains” procedure. As per the procedure, the site should be cordoned off and the remains themselves should be left untouched. The nearest police station and DSDSATSIP are all to be notified as soon as possible. If the human remains are found to be of Aboriginal origin and the police do not wish to investigate the site for criminal activities, the Danggan Balun People should be consulted as to how the remains should be dealt with. Work may only resume after agreement is reached between all notified parties, provided it is in accordance with all parties’ statutory obligations. It is also recommended that in all dealings with Aboriginal human remains, the Proponent should use respectful language, bearing in mind that they are the remains of Aboriginal People rather than scientific specimens.
SourceReference: Partial Clearance Report - Danggan Balun - Ongoing Recommendations

Title: RPP-003
RequirementSummary: The minimum requirements outlined below must be achieved to be eligible for an exemption from having to apply for and obtain a riverine protection permit. - The extent of the area required to carry out the permitted activity must be limited to the m…
Requirement:
The minimum requirements outlined below must be achieved to be eligible for an exemption from having to apply for and obtain a riverine protection permit.
- The extent of the area required to carry out the permitted activity must be limited to the minimum area necessary to reasonably carry out the works.
- Sediment and erosion controls must be used.
- All areas of disturbed bed and banks must be stabilised to protect against erosion.
- All fill placed must be free from contamination (e.g. weeds seeds, oils, chemicals and other contaminants).
- Disturbed banks must be returned to a profile similar to the pre-disturbance condition.
- Natural stream bed controls or features that create natural waterholes (e.g. riffles, logs, sediment or rock bars) must not be lowered or removed.
- Any excavated material that is not removed as waste must be spread evenly within the bed and banks of the watercourse so that it does not interfere with the flow of water.
- All fill placed in the bed of the stream must not redirect flow into an adjacent bank.
- Access tracks or crossings must not interfere with the low flow of water.
- The invert of culverts or the deck height of a splash through crossing must be placed at or below bed level.
- All culverts placed within the watercourse must be aligned with the stream channel and placed as close to the centre of the watercourse channel as practical.
- All culverts placed within the watercourse must be of a sufficient size to ensure uninterrupted low flows and minimise the occurrence of blockage of culverts caused by flood-borne debris.
- Constructed access tracks (e.g. culverts or splash through crossings) must be provided with a scour apron and cut off wall on the downstream side sufficient to prevent bed erosion.
- All disturbed areas must be revegetated with trees, shrub and grasses endemic to the area, sufficient to re-establish a riparian environment and protect bed and banks from erosion.
SourceReference: Riverine protection permit exemption requirements - Section 4.0 Minimum requirements

RequirementSummary: The following guiding principles shall be considered when managing vegetation in order to realise safe, efficient and reliable rail and network operations: - Establish and maintain a risk based approach to vegetation management on the rail corridor.…
Requirement:
The following guiding principles shall be considered when managing vegetation in order to realise safe, efficient and reliable rail and network operations:
- Establish and maintain a risk based approach to vegetation management on the rail corridor.
- Minimise vegetation related interruptions to network availability, including energy supply.
- Adopt vegetation management practices which complement wildfire prevention strategies.
- Establish vegetation management practices which appropriately balance safety, reliability and costs, with community expectations and ecological values.
- Ensure maintenance of safe clearances between vegetation and electric traction infrastructure and other rail infrastructure.
- Ensure environmental issues including amenity, erosion, wildlife habitat and breeding places, weed spread and risk of wildfires are considered in vegetation management.
- Ensure all workers and contractors have the training, knowledge, skills and qualifications they need to undertake their work in a safe, effective, and environmentally responsible manner.
- Consider alternative options or techniques when proposing removal or pruning of vegetation whenever practicable.
- Comply with all relevant legislation, regulations, standards, codes and licences.
SourceReference: MD-15-3 (1.2) Vegetation Management Standard - Section 2.4 Vegetation management guiding principles

Title: SPEC-031
RequirementSummary: The Biosecurity Act 2014 (Qld) establishes a General Biosecurity Obligation (GBO) on all persons who deals with a biosecurity matter (including invasive weeds). Under the GBO, Queensland Rail activities which pose a biosecurity risk must: 1) take al…
Requirement:
The Biosecurity Act 2014 (Qld) establishes a General Biosecurity Obligation (GBO) on all persons who deals with a biosecurity matter (including invasive weeds). Under the GBO, Queensland Rail activities which pose a biosecurity risk must:
1) take all reasonable and practical steps to prevent or minimise each biosecurity risk
2) minimise the likelihood of causing a biosecurity event, and limit the consequences if such an event is caused
3) prevent or minimise the harmful effects a risk could have, and not do anything that might make any harmful effects worse.
Queensland Rail will manage invasive weeds within its property boundaries, using appropriate methods including chemical, physical and/or mechanical methods.
SourceReference: MD-15-3 (1.2) Vegetation Management Standard - Section 2.11 Weed management

Title: SPEC-032
RequirementSummary: Revegetation projects should utilise plants native to the local area where practical and cognisant of the end land use. Landscaping projects for beautification particularly around buildings or precincts, should also consider native species. Suitabil…
Requirement:
Revegetation projects should utilise plants native to the local area where practical and cognisant of the end land use.
Landscaping projects for beautification particularly around buildings or precincts, should also consider native species.
Suitability of plant species must consider a range of matters inclusive of vegetation height, form and habit; potential leaf/ branch/ seed/ flower drop hazards; watering requirements; and general maintenance requirements.
Fauna attraction should also be considered so as not to introduce an unnecessary environmental, safety or operational hazard.
A qualified or experienced horticulturalist, landscape architect and/or botanist/ecologist can assist with species selection and design.
SourceReference: MD-15-3 (1.2) Vegetation Management Standard - Section 2.12 Landscaping and revegetation
